## **Understanding Your Right to Request Medical Records from Baylor Scott & White Health**


### **The Importance of Your Medical History**


Medical records are the foundation of personal injury litigation. Treatment notes, imaging, billing statements, and physician assessments document injuries, establish causation, and quantify damages, so incomplete or delayed records directly affect case value and settlement timelines.


Under HIPAA, providers generally must act on a patient access request within 30 calendar days, with one permitted extension of up to 30 additional calendar days if the required written notice is provided, according to[HHS access guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/how-timely-must-a-covered-entity-be/index.html) . More protective state requirements may apply. This patient-access framework doesn't automatically govern every attorney authorization request.


### **Legal Framework for Record Access**


The Texas Medical Records Privacy Act (Health & Safety Code Chapter 181), Texas Occupations Code § 159.006, and Texas Health and Safety Code § 241.154 shape the state-specific framework for medical record requests. Key provisions include:


-


**Hospital requests:** Under the[Texas hospital statute](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/HS/htm/HS.241.htm) , hospitals generally must act by the 15th calendar day after receiving the request and authorized payment, either by providing the records or by notifying the requester that they don't exist or can't be found


-


**Physician requests:** A separate 15-business-day requirement applies


-


**Qualifying patient electronic-access requests:** A separate 15-business-day requirement applies under[§ 181.102](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/HS/htm/HS.181.htm)


-


Patients can request records in electronic format if readily producible


-


Fees are subject to applicable statutory limits


-


BSWH's form states that copies sent directly to another healthcare provider aren't charged, and separate Texas exemptions apply to qualifying disability-related benefits or assistance requests, so confirm eligibility for the specific request


For routine authorization-based attorney requests, use a valid patient authorization. Other disclosure routes may apply, including qualifying court orders and subpoenas that satisfy applicable legal requirements.


## **Navigating Baylor Scott & White's Online Portals for Medical Records**


### **First-Time MyChart Access**


The MyBSWHealth patient portal gives patients digital access to recent medical records. Available as both a[web and mobile app](https://www.bswhealth.com/patient-tools/mybswhealth-patient-portal) for iOS and Android, the portal allows users to:


-


View lab results, medications, and immunization records


-


Access visit summaries and clinical notes


-


Download records in PDF format


-


Message healthcare providers directly


Patients and approved proxies can access information through MyBSWHealth. Historical records may not be complete, so confirm that the available records cover the requested facilities, dates, and document types. For complete multi-facility documentation, formal authorization requests remain the standard route.


### **Troubleshooting Online Record Requests**


Baylor Scott & White Medical Center, Frisco at 5601 Warren Parkway has its own portal and authorization process, separate from the main MyBSWHealth system. Its[published records instructions](https://baylorfrisco.com/patients-and-visitors/patient-information) also accept requests at HIMPORTAL@bmcf.com or by fax at 214.407.5389, along with the completed authorization and photo ID. Don't confuse this hospital with other BSWH facilities in the Frisco area, such as Centennial or Frisco at PGA Parkway, which may follow different instructions.


BSWH Emergency Hospitals (locations in Aubrey, Burleson, Colleyville, Grand Prairie, Keller, Mansfield, Murphy, and Rockwall) follow a separate process too. They direct attorney and third-party liability requests to the[SmartRequest portal](https://bsweh.org/patient-info) rather than the standard HealthMark Group channels, and they also list fax 307.462.0239 and a status line at 800.367.1500.


## **Required Forms: Baylor Scott & White Medical Records Request and HIPAA Authorizations**


### **Downloading the Correct Forms**


Baylor Scott & White provides four versions of its authorization form:


-


Authorization for Release of Information FROM BSWH (English)


-


Authorization for Release of Information TO BSWH (English)


-


Authorization for Release of Information FROM BSWH (Spanish)


-


Authorization for Release of Information TO BSWH (Spanish)


For legal requests, use the "FROM BSWH" version, which authorizes release to you or your firm. Download it from the[BSWH records page](https://www.bswhealth.com/patient-tools/request-copies-of-your-medical-records) .


### **Key Sections to Complete on Your Authorization**


A complete authorization form should include:


**Patient Information:**


-


Full legal name (verify that the maiden or married name matches the medical records)


-


Date of birth


-


Current address and phone number


-


Account number or MRN if available


-


The originating BSWH facility


**Recipient Information:**


-


Name of the receiving attorney or firm


-


Recipient address


-


Purpose of the disclosure


**Request Specifications:**


-


Specific date range for records (from X date to Y date)


-


Types of records requested (clinic notes, labs, radiology, discharge summary, billing)


-


Delivery method (the form distinguishes delivery options, including fax to a healthcare provider)


**Sensitive Record Authorizations:**


BSWH's form requests separate initials for applicable:


-


Alcohol and drug treatment records


-


Genetic testing information


-


HIV/AIDS information


-


Mental health records


Additional legal restrictions may apply depending on the records and the disclosure purpose.


**Signature Requirements:**


-


Patient signature (or legal representative with supporting documentation)


-


Date signed


-


Expiration date (the form's default is 180 days from signature; for ongoing litigation, specify "conclusion of legal case" as the triggering event)


Missing required information can delay or invalidate the request. Complete the applicable fields and supporting documentation, and ask the records department about any uncertainty.

## **Retrieving Old Medical Records from Baylor Scott & White Facilities**


### **Challenges in Retrieving Older Records**


Texas physician records generally must be kept for seven years after the last treatment; for minors, until age 21 or seven years after the last treatment, whichever is later. Hospital records generally have a 10-year retention period after the last treatment. For hospital patients last treated as minors, the period extends until age 20 or 10 years after the last treatment, whichever is later. Additional preservation requirements can apply. (TMB physician rules now sit in Chapter 163.)


Archived records can be harder to locate. Common challenges include:


-


Records stored in different formats or systems following facility mergers


-


Patient name changes not reflected in older documentation


-


Incomplete date ranges when treatment spanned multiple calendar years


-


Imaging studies stored on outdated media formats


### **Best Practices for Historical Record Requests**


When requesting older records:


1.


Verify the correct facility name at the time of treatment (facilities may have changed names or merged)


2.


Provide account numbers from billing statements to help locate archived records


3.


Include all known name variations the patient may have used


4.


Request specific date ranges rather than "all records" to focus the search


5.


Correct deficiencies promptly and document when a valid request and any required payment were received, rather than assuming archived records automatically qualify for extra time

HIPAA's Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164) sets federal standards for access to protected health information. Key points for legal professionals include:


-


Routine attorney requests generally rely on a valid, signed patient authorization, though qualifying court orders and subpoenas are other routes


-


Authorization forms must include specific elements, including an expiration date


-


Sensitive categories need separate initials on BSWH's form, and additional legal restrictions may apply


-


Patient-access fees follow separate HIPAA rules from third-party request fees


### **Who Can Access Your Medical Records?**


Follow the receiving facility's identity-verification instructions and provide documentation establishing the representative's authority when applicable. Common scenarios include:


-


**Legal representatives:** A signed patient authorization, plus any ID the facility requests (Baylor Frisco asks for photo ID)


-


**Minor patient records:** A parent or guardian, with documentation of authority when the facility requires it


-


**Deceased patient records:** The personal representative of the estate, with documentation establishing that authority (a death certificate alone doesn't establish it)


-


**Power of attorney holders:** Valid POA documentation covering healthcare decisions

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How long does it typically take to receive medical records from Baylor Scott & White Health?**


It depends on the provider and request type. Hospital requests generally fall under a 15-calendar-day requirement after receipt of the request and authorized payment, while physician requests and qualifying patient electronic-access requests have separate 15-business-day requirements. Confirm receipt and expected completion with the records department, and don't assume every rejection restarts the deadline. With Codes Health, firms typically receive complete, organized records in a couple of weeks.


### **Can I request medical records for a family member from Baylor Scott & White?**


Yes, with the right documentation. For adult family members, you need the patient's signed HIPAA authorization, a valid healthcare power of attorney, or guardianship documentation. Parents or guardians of minors and estate representatives should document their authority when applicable. A death certificate alone doesn't establish authority over an estate. Follow the receiving facility's identity-verification instructions, since requirements such as photo ID can vary by facility.


### **Is there a fee for requesting medical records from Baylor Scott & White Health?**


Usually, yes. Hospital charges depend on the request, format, exemptions, and current statutory limits, so ask for an itemized estimate first. For physician records, Texas caps paper copies at $25 for the first 20 pages plus $0.50 per page after, and electronic copies at $25 for up to 500 pages and $50 for more than 500 pages, per the[Texas physician fee limits](https://capitol.texas.gov/tlodocs/85R/analysis/html/SB01520I.htm) . Affidavit fees are separate, and patient-access fees follow separate HIPAA rules. BSWH's form states that copies sent directly to another healthcare provider aren't charged, and separate Texas exemptions apply to qualifying disability-related benefits or assistance requests, so confirm eligibility for your specific request.


### **What is the difference between a medical records request form and a HIPAA authorization form?**


A medical records request form typically captures what records you want, from which dates, and how you want them delivered. A HIPAA authorization form grants permission for a covered entity to release protected health information to a specified third party. BSWH combines both in its Authorization for Release of Information form, covering the patient, recipient, records requested, purpose, delivery, sensitive-record initials, expiration, and signature. Qualifying court orders and subpoenas can be other disclosure routes.


### **What should I do if Baylor Scott & White denies or delays my medical records request?**


First, contact HealthMark Group at 844.848.2794 (or the facility that received your request) to find out why. Common issues include incomplete or expired authorizations, missing requested documentation, or trouble locating the patient's records. If the authorization is incomplete, get a corrected form from your client right away and document when the valid request and any required payment were received. If records still aren't delivered, escalate in writing to the records department or privacy officer, identifying the applicable request type and deadline. Hospital requests generally require reference to § 241.154, while physician and patient electronic-access requests involve different provisions. Keep a record of all communications throughout.
